274453859.description:
Glass Insulator Lot - 3 Pieces
Hemingray, No. 42 Pattern
Aqua and Clear, Vintage
This collection features three vintage American glass insulators, including two in the classic aqua blue-green color and one in clear glass. These No. 42 telegraph insulators were a staple of American infrastructure throughout the mid-20th century, produced by the Hemingray Glass Company. They are highly collected for their architectural form and the way they capture and refract light in display settings.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Aqua, Hemingray No. 42, Made in U.S.A., Drip points on base - Minor edge fleabites
Glass Insulator, Aqua, Hemingray No. 42, Made in U.S.A., Drip points on base - Minor base roughness
Glass Insulator, Clear, No. 45 mark on base ring, Tapered design - Surface wear and inner haze
Condition:
Overall very good vintage condition. The aqua pieces show typical minor roughness and small fleabites on the bottom drip points, which is common for authentic used insulators. The clear piece shows some light surface scratches and internal cloudiness or residue. No large structural cracks or major damage observed. Original manufacturing bubbles and swirl marks are present within the glass, adding to the vintage character.

274793973.description:
Orthoceras Fossil Specimen Polished Nautiloid Cephalopod Shell Display
This fossil specimen features two Orthoceras fossils embedded in a dark gray to black matrix rock. Orthoceras is an extinct genus of nautiloid cephalopod characterized by long, tapered, conical shells with visible internal chamber lines. The matrix rock is rough and unpolished on the back and sides, while the fossilized shells on the front are polished to a glossy finish, highlighting their natural details and structure. The piece is in excellent natural condition with no visible repairs, suitable for fossil collectors or natural history displays.
Product Size:
10 x 4 x 4 in
2.2 lb
